minutes.headline: Building committee finalized interview questions for the design firm, set a Nov 20 interview, and approved two sets of minutes.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a resident question why Town Hall would hold meeting rooms rather than offices and what relocating the PACT broadcast feed would cost. It then reviewed, reworded and reordered interview questions for the design firm Taylor and Burns. It approved the October 21 and November 4 minutes by roll call and adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Asked what Comcast quoted to relocate the PACT broadcast feed to TCP. Questioned making 6,500 sq ft of Town Hall into meeting rooms and the need for the 4,000 sq ft Ritter Annex, and suggested using Town Hall as office space.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of October 21st and November 4th.
votes.outcome: passed (roll call; Tom Gray, Brian, Dave, Tony and the chair each said aye)

budget_items.topic: Cost of relocating PACT broadcast feed / cabling to TCP
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the earlier cost referred to cabling from many meeting rooms back to a studio, and that PACT brings its own funds to outfit its space. The chair will get back on the quoted amount.

budget_items.topic: PACT funds and Xfinity broadcast fees
budget_items.what_was_said: Tony said PACT earns money from the Xfinity agreement, which runs through about 2028, and holds a sum he put between half a million and a million dollars. Moving the feed point could require paying for a new location.
figures_as_heard: over a half million but less than a million dollars

budget_items.topic: Meeting room space, future-proofing and change of use
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said a partition is cheaper than a new building, and that keeping an office in Town Hall avoids a change of use that could trigger code upgrades.

decisions.decision: The chair will schedule the Taylor and Burns interview for next Wednesday at 5:30 and contact them in the morning.
Trinity Episcopal question reworded to ask neutrally about the design process, with a follow-up about the initial demolition plan if needed.
The question on the Park Service preservation emails was dropped, question four was moved to the end as a time-permitting question, and the order was revised.
A space-needs review will be planned after the interview, and members suggested it may need more than 45 minutes or an extra meeting.
Next meeting set for the 20th at 5:30 for interviews, with a kickoff on December 2nd and later dates of December 16th and in January.

what_happened.line: The Municipal Building Design Committee finalized, reworded and reordered its interview questions for the design firm Taylor and Burns.
The chair will schedule the Taylor and Burns interview for next Wednesday at 5:30 and contact the firm in the morning.
A resident asked what was quoted to relocate the PACT broadcast feed; the chair said the earlier cost was for cabling and will follow up on the amount.
A space-needs review is planned after the interview, and members said it may need more than 45 minutes or an extra meeting.
The committee approved two sets of minutes by roll call and set the next meeting for the 20th at 5:30.

why_it_matters: This committee is choosing the design firm that will shape how Town Hall and related buildings are used, so the interview questions set what residents learn about cost, preservation and space before a design is proposed.
The unanswered question about moving the PACT broadcast feed is a possible cost to the project, and any building funding request residents are later asked to vote on would need to account for it.
watch_next: The Taylor and Burns interview, set for the next Wednesday at 5:30 (the minutes also list the 20th at 5:30 for interviews).
The chair's follow-up on the quoted cost to relocate the PACT feed, and the December 2 kickoff meeting.
